description: We are a team of students passionate about science, technology, programming, and innovation. We are excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to collaborate, share ideas, and develop creative solutions to real-world problems.
summary:
AgriSmart is a smart agricultural application developed to address the Field Shift challenge by helping farmers adapt their farming decisions to changing environmental conditions.

The application uses the farmer's GPS location, selected crop, and soil type to analyze agricultural suitability using NASA data, including temperature, expected rainfall, and humidity. Farmers can also use the camera feature to identify their soil type. Based on this analysis, AgriSmart recommends suitable crops and alternative crop rotation options when the selected crop is not appropriate for the local environment.

In addition, we developed a physical smart irrigation device using an Arduino Uno, a soil moisture sensor, and a water pump. It automatically supplies water when the soil needs it and stops when the required moisture level is reached.

AgriSmart aims to support sustainable agriculture, reduce water waste, improve crop productivity, and help farmers make data-driven decisions. Our future plans include adding sensors to monitor soil nutrients and provide fertilizer recommendations.
details:
AgriSmart is a smart agricultural solution designed to help farmers make better decisions about crop selection, crop rotation, and water management using NASA data.

The application allows farmers to enter their farm location using GPS, select the crop they want to grow, and identify their soil type. If farmers do not know their soil type, we propose using an AI-powered camera feature to analyze a soil image and identify its type.

The application uses NASA environmental data, including temperature, rainfall, and humidity, to analyze the suitability of the selected crop for the farm's conditions. It then provides recommendations for suitable crops and alternative crop rotation options to improve agricultural productivity and reduce risks.

Our project also includes a physical irrigation prototype built using an Arduino Uno, a soil moisture sensor, a relay module, and a water pump. The sensor measures soil moisture, and the Arduino controls the pump to provide water when needed and stop irrigation when the required moisture level is reached.

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web application, and Arduino IDE with C++ for programming the hardware.

The creativity of our project comes from combining NASA environmental data, smart agricultural recommendations, and a real physical irrigation system in one solution.

Our team considered several important factors, including geographical location, soil type, crop requirements, temperature, rainfall, humidity, water availability, and soil moisture.

Our intended impact is to support sustainable agriculture, reduce water waste, help farmers make informed decisions, and improve crop productivity, especially in areas facing water scarcity and changing environmental conditions.
